## The problem

Practice building analytics end to end in the cloud on a job postings dataset
that is too large for a spreadsheet, and turn it into clear answers about pay
and demand.

## What I did

- Set up an AWS EC2 instance with PySpark, a Python virtual environment and a
  Git workflow, and worked on it remotely from VS Code.
- Modeled the postings as a star schema in Spark SQL and wrote four queries on
  salary and demand across industries and states.
- Converted hourly, weekly and monthly pay to annual salaries and bounded
  outliers at the 99.5th percentile.
- Cleaned state names with a lookup table that fixed abbreviations and split
  city names.
- In a second analysis, recovered years of experience from job description
  text with regular expressions when the structured fields were empty, then
  charted salary by industry, education, experience and remote status.
- Added swap space after Spark ran out of memory on the full dataset.

## Results

Reproducible reports rendered to HTML, Word and PDF from one Quarto source,
with interactive charts on the web and static images in the documents.

## What I learned

Working at scale changes your habits. I now check data quality before modeling,
keep the raw data untouched and expect infrastructure issues, like memory and
sessions, to be part of the job rather than a surprise.

*The code stays private under the course's academic integrity policy.*
